MyHeritage is being searched for a marriage record for Patrick Flynn in Pennsylvania, around 1865 to 1875. Open this search:

**[MyHeritage Search — Patrick Flynn, Pennsylvania Marriage](https://www.myheritage.com/research?s=1&formId=master&formMode=1&useTranslation=1&exactSearch=&p=1&action=query&view_mode=card&qname=Name+fn.Patrick+fnmo.1+ln.Flynn+lnmsrs.false&qevents-event1=Event+et.any+ep.Pennsylvania%2C+United+States+epmo.similar&qevents=List)**

This could reveal his wife's name and the place and date of their marriage. A few things to note:

- **Marriage years**: The link can't pre-set a year range — once the page loads, enter **1865–1875** in the site's own form.
- **Login may be required**: The file shows Ancestry as your subscription; MyHeritage may hit a login wall or show limited previews.
- **Many results expected**: MyHeritage ranks rather than filters, so there may be a lot of hits — look for a Patrick Flynn born around 1845.
- **FamilySearch alternative**: FamilySearch holds *Pennsylvania, Civil Marriages, 1677–1950* and *Pennsylvania, Compiled Marriages, 1700–1900*, which can be searched through search-records if you prefer.

**Next step**: After the page loads, save it as a PDF (Ctrl+P → Save as PDF on Windows) and upload it here. The results will be triaged to identify which records are the right Patrick Flynn.

items.description: Patrick Flynn's birthplace: Ireland (1850 and 1860 censuses) vs. Pennsylvania (1908 death certificate)
items.independence_analysis: The two census records (1850, 1860) are independent original sources with different enumerators. The death certificate is a third independent original source. However, the census informants are likely the same household member (Thomas Flynn or wife), so the two census assertions may share a single informant — potentially not fully independent for this fact.
items.weighing_analysis: The census records are contemporary recordings made near the time of Patrick's birth, while the death certificate was created 63 years later. The census informant was likely a household member with firsthand knowledge (primary or indeterminate), while the death certificate informant (son-in-law) is clearly secondary for birth facts. Two contemporary sources outweigh one later recollection by a secondary informant.
items.resolution_rationale: Ireland is accepted as the birthplace. The 1908 death certificate birthplace of 'Pennsylvania' is rejected as a likely error by the son-in-law informant, who may have confused Patrick's place of residence with his place of birth, or may not have known Patrick was born in Ireland before immigrating as a young child.

items.rationale: Confirm Patrick still in Thomas Flynn household in 1860. Strengthens parent-child identification.

output.text_response:
I searched the 1855 Massachusetts State Census on MyHeritage for Josiah Barnes, and the capture showed two results:

1. **Strong match — Josiah Barnes**, born about 1818 in Massachusetts, enumerated in Lexington, Middlesex County. Household: Lucy (b. ~1821), Henry (b. ~1844), Mary (b. ~1847).
2. **No match — Josiah Barnes**, born about 1817 in New Hampshire, Lowell, MA. Birthplace is wrong; almost certainly a different man.

The search has been logged (log_002, closing the prior hand-off log_001) and plan item **pli_001** is now complete. This is an index entry only — the original census page still needs checking.

**Next steps:**
1. Open the Lexington entry on MyHeritage and capture the full record page (PDF or screenshot).
2. Hand that capture to the **record-structurer** agent to extract the facts as a source.
3. After that, run **research-exhaustiveness** — all planned searches are now complete.
